newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Overnight guilders hold onto highs, long end eases.
newsitem.headline: Overnight guilders hold onto highs, long end eases.

text.p: Overnight guilders stayed pinned to the previous day's relatively high levels in a slack Wednesday session as players covered themselves ahead of next week's government bond payments.
Call money was quoted at 2.87-88 percent bid with most deals being done around these levels, dealers said. This compares to a rate on special advances of just 2.50 percent.

The rates reflected a slightly skewed liquidity distribution among market players as well as the building up of positions in anticipation of Monday's payment date on the latest Dutch government bond issue, dealers said.
Six-month to one-year guilder rates eased fractionally.
Dealers said this was due to guilder offerings in the Euromarket, where arbitrage was undermining rates.
The Dutch currency was quoting at 1.8845/50 against the dollar on Wednesday, a touch softer than its Tuesday fixing.
However it was firmer against the mark at 112.22 per 100 marks, compared with Tuesday's 112.27 fixing.
